newsitem.title: UK: IPE details new limits on gas oil futures position.
newsitem.headline: IPE details new limits on gas oil futures position.

text.p: Tough new rules limiting the size of gas oil futures positions ahead of expiry have been approved in principle by the board of London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), the exchange said on Wednesday.
The IPE said in a statement that the new rules accept in full most of the recommendations made in an independent study it commissioned from consultant Sally Clubley.
The study was commissioned in January folowing a damaging squeeze in the gas oil contract last November.
The IPE said it also incorporated feedback from the industry and conducted its own research.
The main changes are listed below:
1. The IPE intends to extend client level position monitoring to four weeks before expiry of the delivery month. Clients should not exceed the following levels of open interest.
0-5 business days before expiry a total of 3,500 lots.
6-10 business days before expiry a total of 7,000 lots.
11-15 business days before expiry a total of 12,500 lots.
Exemptions to these levels will only be considered under exceptional circumstances.

2. The IPE will impose a new selective excessive position levy (EPL) if the levels described above are exceeded. The EPL will be a percentage of the contract value and would apply to the whole position, not just the excess. The EPL will be payable in cash ony and interest would not be awarded. The rate will depend on the time left before expiry.
0-5 business days before expiry EPL set at 100 percent of the contract value.
6-10 business days before expiry EPL set at 50 percent of the contract value.
11-15 business days before expiry EPL set at 25 percent of the contract value.

Fines on each lot over the relevant level would also be levied each day the level is exceeded. The level of the fine has yet to be determined but it is envisaged that 10 pounds sterling per lot will be appropriate.

If in spite of these preventative measures a position is maintained in excess of prescribed levels the IPE may enforce liquidation of part of a position. This proposal is subject to the approval of London Clearing House (LCH).
3. The IPE will appoint a delivery committee made up of IPE members and trade representatives to adjudicate on delivery dsiputes.
Details of these proposals will be examined by the IPE's Membership and Rules Committee and will also require approval from the appropriate regulatory authority.
